newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Salomon rates Chernogorneft a buy.
newsitem.headline: Salomon rates Chernogorneft a buy.

text.p: Russian oil company Chernogorneft is poised for longer-term growth and, despite a recent price rally, the stock is undervalued and could rise further if the industry recovers, Salomon Brothers said.
Salomon said in a report that it was reiterating its buy recommendation on Chernogorneft, part of the Sidanko vertically-integrated oil company.
Chernogorneft's financial performance in 1996 should be roughly in line with last year's and the company is seeking to stabilise production, Salomon said.

It said the recent credit ratings awarded to Russia and falls in yields on MinFin bonds had prompted it to lower its discount rate in cash flow analysis of Chernogorneft to 20 percent from 30 percent.

Taking into account other information disclosed by the company, a tax restructuring deal and other factors, Salomon said it had raised its "base-case valuation" of Chernogorneft to $500 million, or $18.60 a share, from $340 million.
"The shares offer even greater upside in the event of an industry recovery, with higher domestic oil prices and a reduced tax burden," Salomon said.

In many Russian oil companies, stock in subsidiaries is being converted into shares of the parent. Salomon said Sidanko had no clear integration strategy and that Chernogorneft was likely to remain independent for the next year or two.

Salomon said the risk to investors from a conversion of Chernogorneft was lower than in some companies because Sidanko needed huge investment and this would be unlikely to happen in a company which disregarded shareholder rights.
Apart from this, a share conversion would require the approval of 75 percent of shareholders. Foreign investors, with nearly 32 percent of the company, would have an important voice. Salomon said.
Chrnogorneft were bid at $11.50 on Wednesday.
